newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TASMANIA ON VERGE OF EASY SHIELD WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TASMANIA ON VERGE OF EASY SHIELD WIN.

text.p: Tasmania moved into a commanding position on the third day of their Sheffield Shield match against South Australia on Monday after reducing the defending champions to 127 for six in their second innings.
Tasmania, who have never won the competition, were earlier dismissed for 425 after resuming on 304 for six to take a first innings lead of 132 at the Adelaide Oval.

While the match had been evenly poised overnight after South Australia's first innings of 293, middle-order batsmen Daniel Marsh and Mark Atkinson swung the match decisively Tasmania's way with a seventh-wicket partnership of 118.
Marsh, the son of former Australia wicketkeeper Rod Marsh, and Atkinson both made 58.
Tasmania's bowlers then strengthened their side's grip on the match, with pacemen Colin Miller and Josh Marquet taking two wickets each as South Australia slumped to 76 for four.
Tail-enders Geoff Parker and Brad Young were at the crease, Parker on 34 and Young on one.

South Australia lie bottom of the Shield standings on six points from one win in six matches this season. Tasmania are one place higher in fifth on 12 points but can leap-frog Victoria into fourth by closing out a win on Tuesday's final day of play.
